label: Cell-resolved premise: PDH restraint must be read per cell class, because the dominant kinase differs by class and species
observation (DATO): RNA: mouse cortical neurons Pdk2 first (13.75 FPKM of 25.5), human cortical neurons PDK3 first (cortex-only 59.6-121.1 nCPM against PDK2 16.2-31.4), astrocytes PDK4 first in mouse and human (human mature 22.59 against 7.52 FPKM, 12 patients), human oligodendrocytes PDK4 first, mouse oligodendrocyte lineage Pdk2 first with Pdk3 second; PDK4 in human astrocytes rises with maturation (fetal 1.42, adult 22.59); protein only coarse IHC (D01-D04, D06, D07)
relation (INFERENZA): A bulk lysate from a mixed culture or organoid averages classes whose restraining kinase differs; a null or a rise of PDH phosphorylation in bulk cannot say which cell carries it. An RNA share is not an activity share (INFERENZA)
proposed_action (IPOTESI): Run the INV-07 step 2 on marker-resolved or sorted material: PDH E1-alpha amount, phosphorylation at the three sites, activity before and after dephosphorylation, and PDK3 and PDK4 (and PDK2) transcript and protein per cell class, in the same lysates as INV-19
favourable_context: Human neural material with neurons (PDK3-dominant) and astrocytes or oligodendrocyte lineage (PDK4-dominant) separable; mixed organoid
opposite_context: A mouse neuronal preparation (PDK2-dominant) read as if it carried the human neuronal result; a bulk sample read for one class
expected_functional_result: A decision about which class, if any, carries a PDH restraint; no functional claim
refuting_measure: Equal phosphorylation difference and equal kinase transcripts in every class would make the cell-resolved design unnecessary (then the bulk measurement suffices)
class: new combination in the repository (isoform-by-cell-class input to the INV-07 premise); literature novelty not assessed
consumer: need NEED-PDH-PYRUVATE-AXIS (premise measurement text); INV-07 next_test; INV-19 shared lysate note

label: Tool by isoform: the first probe is chosen by the dominant kinase and by the scaffold condition, with a genetic arm as reference
observation (DATO): AZD7545: core-bound inhibition of human PDK1 (IC50 87 nM) and PDK3 (0.60 uM); core-free stimulation of PDK1 (marginal), PDK3 (10-fold) and PDK4 (2.8-fold); PDK2 not measured in any source opened (the repository 8.19 and its species unverified). VER-246608: IC50 35, 84, 40, 91 nM on four constructs, E1-only DELFIA, ATP-competitive; raises lysate PDH activity in PC-3 cells (about 140 percent, raster read). DCA: millimolar, isoform-dependent in vitro (A3D01-A3D10)
relation (INFERENZA): The sign of a lipoamide-site compound depends on whether the kinase sits on its E2/E3BP scaffold; in PDK4-dominant cells (astrocytes, human oligodendrocytes) AZD7545 has only core-free stimulation on record, so its sign there is unmeasured, not 'inhibitor' (A3D05, corrected)
proposed_action (IPOTESI): In the premise cells use two chemically unrelated probes at matched PDH phosphorylation change (VER-246608 as the ATP-site, all-isoform probe; DCA as the pyruvate-site reference at its own concentration) and a genetic knockdown of the dominant isoform; AZD7545 only as a scaffold-sign probe read with the phospho-readout
favourable_context: A restraint is measured in a cell class and the dominant kinase there has a tool row
opposite_context: No restraint is measured; the cell class expresses a kinase the tool has no core-bound row on (AZD7545 and PDK4)
expected_functional_result: Agreement of the two chemotypes and the genetic arm on the phosphorylation and activity change supports a PDK-dependent effect; disagreement points to a compound-specific action or the scaffold
refuting_measure: AZD7545 lowering PDH phosphorylation in a PDK4-dominant class would remove the scaffold-sign concern for that class; VER-246608 failing to change phosphorylation where the genetic arm does would show a construct or cell-entry limit
class: known but unused (the primary pharmacology was held as abstract values); new combination for the comparison path
consumer: compound view (DCA, VER-246608, AZD7545 roles); comparison engine inputs (engine/)

label: Two directions of one lever: PDK lowering may raise oxidation in neurons and lower lactate export from PDK4-dominant astrocytes, with the burst as the functional endpoint
observation (DATO): Astrocyte Ldha loss lowered lactate and firing in adult mouse dmPFC (GFAP-Cre knockout, progenitor origin; AAV astrocyte arm: firing and lactate only) and neuronal MCT2 was needed for the lactate effect (A4D04, A4D05); oxamate shortened status epilepticus in adult mice and lowered CA1 calcium activity and sEPSC frequency (A4D01, A4D02); the Wwox KO slice shows bursts in 36 of 42 slices (INV-07/INV-18 records)
relation (INFERENZA): If excitability in the burst depends on lactate supply, a lactate-side reduction lowers it; PDK inhibition acts on the opposite end of the same node (more pyruvate oxidation, less lactate). The sign of net benefit by class is unknown (INFERENZA)
proposed_action (IPOTESI): In the KO slice, at matched suppression of the burst, compare an LDH inhibitor, a lactate-transport probe and a receptor route, each with pyruvate add-back; record burst incidence, resting Vm and Rin, and extracellular lactate
favourable_context: Burst incidence falls with the lactate-side tool and returns with pyruvate or lactate add-back, at a suppression level matched to the receptor route
opposite_context: The burst is unchanged by the lactate-side tool; or lowering lactate worsens a readout (depressive-like behaviour in the Ldha model is a documented harm direction)
expected_functional_result: Whether the metabolic step is necessary or only coincident for the burst; no clinical preference or substitution is implied
refuting_measure: A burst that does not respond to the lactate-side tool at an achieved block (measured) refutes the lactate-supply dependence for that preparation
class: new combination in the repository; literature novelty not assessed
consumer: open question (lactate supply and burst); INV-07 comparison rows; INV-18 K-branch note (PH4)

label: A lactate-closed ATP-sensitive K+ conductance could carry part of the Rin and rest pattern, as a metabolic upstream of the K branch
observation (DATO): Juvenile (P13-24) rat and mouse barrel cortex, layers I-IV: KATP modulators change membrane potential, resistance and firing; diazoxide roughly doubles whole-cell conductance; in perforated patch 15 mM lactate with 2.5 mM glucose roughly doubles firing, absent in Kcnj11 knockout; the pooled cells are not split by type (34766906, verifier read; abstract-level companion work: BHB, GIRK, A-type, M-current) (verify/v2 item 1). Wwox KO layer II/III: Rin +39 percent, rest +5.6 mV, an implied reversal near -94 mV (SCI43); lactate is raised in WWOX-related non-neural and fly systems and in one individual (INV-07)
relation (INFERENZA): Lactate closes KATP (a conductance loss with an E_K reversal) and so fits the sign and the implied reversal of the Rin and rest change; a KATP loss is also Ba2+-sensitive and tool-rich (INFERENZA). The Wwox recordings were K-gluconate whole-cell with 2 mM Na2ATP in the pipette (held audit A1.15 of the Wwox Methods, found at the coda recheck on 2026-11-11), so a lactate-closed KATP loss is unlikely to be the main carrier of the published values; the hypothesis stands for ATP-undisturbed recordings
proposed_action (IPOTESI): Same-cell design: perforated or cell-attached recording with ATP undisturbed; diazoxide and a sulfonylurea in Wwox KO against wild type; occlusion (a KO with closed KATP shows a smaller sulfonylurea effect and a larger diazoxide effect); lactate or pyruvate add-back and LDH-inhibitor arms in the same cells
favourable_context: Perforated-patch recordings in KO and wild-type layer II/III neurons with lactate measured in the same slice (the published whole-cell recordings used 2 mM Na2ATP)
opposite_context: Whole-cell dialysed ATP; wild-type KATP already closed (the authors infer almost closed in juvenile dentate cells); a KATP effect equal in both genotypes
expected_functional_result: A diazoxide-sensitive, sulfonylurea-occluded part of the Rin and rest difference would give a metabolic route to the K branch and a defined, tool-rich arm
refuting_measure: No genotype difference in the diazoxide-sensitive current per pF, or equal sulfonylurea effects, refutes a KATP share; this does not touch the Kir/K2P share of SCI43 step 2b
class: new combination in the repository (metabolic premise joined to the SCI43 K branch); literature novelty not assessed
decisive_rows: A4D08-A4D12 (as corrected); SCI43 KH1; Wwox Table 1
consumer: INV-18 branch D (SCI43 ladder step 2b: add a KATP arm); needs (premise conditions: pipette ATP); IT44 K-branch consumers

label: Risk arm: lowering PDK may do nothing or worsen a compensatory state where PDH is not restrained or PDK induction protects
observation (DATO): Kinase transcript not up in the KO organoid (PDK1 not up, PDHA1 up); non-neural fibroblast PDH activity unchanged; DCA alone or pyruvate alone did not raise neuron counts in rat pilocarpine seizure (only the combination did); DCA slightly proconvulsant in the 6 Hz mouse test (abstract); DCA lowered myelin proteins in Schwann cell and DRG co-cultures (abstract; peripheral); the one randomised human trial of DCA (a mitochondrial disease) stopped early for peripheral neuropathy (abstract); PDK2 and PDK3 documented in neurons; no CNS oligodendrocyte-lineage test found (D08-D13, D16, A3D10)
relation (INFERENZA): PDH release adds NADH and load on a respiratory chain with an unmeasured limit and removes lactate export; a restraint that is protective is removed. Direction by class unknown (INFERENZA)
proposed_action (IPOTESI): Include the lever as a negative control for harm in any arm that tests a PDK lowering: burst incidence, viability, lactate and redox state, with genetic and pharmacological arms
favourable_context: PDH phosphorylation and a functional readout move together in the expected direction
opposite_context: PDH already unrestrained; kinase induction compensatory; a lactate-exporting class dependent on glycolysis
expected_functional_result: Worsening or no change of a functional readout under a measured PDH release would turn the lever into a documented risk, not a candidate
refuting_measure: A functional improvement under measured PDH release in the same cells would argue against the risk reading in that preparation
class: known but unused (the harm direction was in the records but not attached to the lever)
consumer: compound view (DCA caution); INV-07 next_test (genetic arm first)
